items.summary: New data from the Federal Trade Commission reveal that people reported losing a staggering $3.5 billion to imposter scams in 2025, with reported losses increasing nearly three times since 2020. FTC data also show that people reported imposter scams more than any other fraud category in 2025—nearly one in three fraud reports were about imposter scams. These scams lured consumers through text, phone, email, social media, search engine results and other means. Some of the costliest impersonation scams start with a fake security alert, often from a bank. People are convinced to move money to “protect” it, with their losses often limited only by their available funds. story_ideas.title: Solicitation for Nominations To Serve on the Family Caregiving Advisory Council

story_ideas.angle: A service piece walking a working family caregiver through what the Administration for Community Living's 09/14/26 nomination notice asks for and what the council does, written for people currently providing care rather than for the organizations that usually apply.
story_ideas.hook: The notice published 09/14/26 is the newest item in this run and the one federal document this month that invites an ordinary caregiver in rather than telling them something.
story_ideas.summary: The Administration for Community Living (ACL) seeks nominations for individuals to serve on the Family Caregiving Advisory Council.
story_ideas.consumer: If you are caring for a parent or spouse, read the notice, check what the Family Caregiving Advisory Council covers, and decide whether to nominate yourself or someone in your support group before the solicitation closes.
story_ideas.b2b: Provider and nonprofit policy teams should decide now whether their nominee is a staff expert or a family member they serve, because council composition shapes the caregiving guidance they will be asked to implement.
story_ideas.chart: The underlying file supports an original ranking or trend line.
story_ideas.competitive: One or two monitored publishers have touched it.
story_ideas.why: If nobody who does the work applies, the federal account of family caregiving gets written entirely by people who study it.
story_ideas.note: Localizable: state and local area agencies on aging can be asked how they are circulating the solicitation.

feature_pitch_raw:
**The pattern:** The federal channel through which an unpaid family caregiver's experience reaches policy is, right now, a nomination form with a closing date. The Administration for Community Living published its Solicitation for Nominations To Serve on the Family Caregiving Advisory Council on 09/14/26, the newest item in this run and one no monitored publisher has matched beyond light coverage. ACL is separately marking Malnutrition Awareness Week 09/14-18, an observance whose actual work — noticing that someone has stopped eating, and doing something about it — falls on the same households. And BLS puts home health care services average hourly earnings at $28.04 in July 2026, up 2.0% year over year, which is the price of the help those households would hire instead. Together these say something the 09/11/26 pitch on the Senior Medicare Patrol supplement did not: the paid side of care has a wage series printed monthly, and the unpaid side has a seat that has to be applied for.

**Why it matters:** A family caregiver has no published number attached to them in this run. The paid workforce does: $28.04 an hour in July 2026, rising 2.0% year over year. The Advisory Council is the named place in the federal structure where the unpaid side gets described by someone who has done it, and the consequence of the nominations closing without those people in the pool is that the description gets written by organizations rather than households. That is a small stake in dollars and a large one in whose account of caregiving becomes the official one.

**Why pitch this now:** Nominations are open as of 09/14/26 and nomination solicitations close. Malnutrition Awareness Week runs 09/14-18, giving the piece a dated peg this week rather than next month, and the July 2026 wage figure is the current print.

Working title: "The nomination form that decides who speaks for family caregivers." For adult children and spouses currently providing care, and for the aging-services organizations that will otherwise fill the seats.

- The help you would hire instead now costs $28.04 an hour
